subject: physics
question_text: State the physics principle behind MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) and explain how it helps doctors.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 13 (printed p.144). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: MRI uses nuclear magnetic resonance, hydrogen nuclei align in a strong magnetic field and absorb and re-emit radio waves at a definite frequency, and this gives high-contrast images of soft tissue without ionising radiation, unlike an X-ray or a CT scan.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The principle
lines: hydrogen nuclei in the body line
up in a strong magnetic field and
steps.why: Hydrogen nuclei behave like tiny magnets. A strong magnetic field lines them up, a radio pulse at their own resonant frequency flips them, and as they return to alignment they re-emit radio waves that a scanner detects and turns into an image.
common_mistakes: Naming X-rays or radioactivity as the mechanism; MRI uses neither.
Leaving out the word resonance, which names the effect.
steps.memory_tip: MRI: magnetic field lines up hydrogen nuclei, a radio pulse and its echo build the image.
steps.margin_note: The words magnetic and resonance must both appear for full credit.

steps.label: How it helps
steps.why: Because the signal comes from hydrogen nuclei, which are abundant in soft tissue and water, MRI shows contrast between different soft tissues that an X-ray cannot, and it does this without the ionising radiation an X-ray or a CT scan uses.
common_mistakes: Saying MRI is better than an X-ray, with no reason given.
Claiming MRI uses no radiation at all; radio waves are a form of radiation, only not ionising.
steps.memory_tip: MRI shows soft tissue clearly and safely, since radio waves are not ionising radiation.
steps.margin_note: Naming one example organ or tissue, such as the brain, is accepted as part of this mark.
